questions.note: Order reads right: hallux longest, the 2nd just shorter, 3-5 descending, the 5th curled with its nail turned out. Knuckles and pulps exist, but the lesser toes repeat one smooth sausage with faint, sparse creases, and from below they show a hard seam across toes 3-4 and jagged mask outlines at their bases (V4, hr.plantar).

Five plates with free-edge thickness and a pale crescent at the hallux base, trimmed straight, none floating. But every nail is the same pale opaque pink tile with a bright, even French-tip strip, outlined crisply on the skin with no fold lapping over, no pink bed showing through, no yellowing, wear or grime: press-on nails at native size.

The extensor fan is there and in relief, but drawn as thin hard lines 1-2 mm wide, like wires or scored grooves rather than cords, and the EHL is no broader than the rest. No dorsal venous arch, tributaries or saphenous vein in front of the medial malleolus shows in V1f, V2 or V5f: an unveined, mannequin dorsum.

Shadow sides stay dark and nothing glows, but the colour is one procedural cloud mottle everywhere; toes and dorsum read smooth and slightly waxy at 15-30 px/mm with little cell or pore relief, while the sole has crisp corduroy ridges, target whorls with seams and a Voronoi heel decal with a straight edge.

defects.what: Heel callus is a flat cream patch over the whole plantar heel, cut off by a ruler-straight transverse edge and printed with an even Voronoi crack net: a texture decal, not thickened skin.
defects.fix: Real heel callus is a raised rim band thickest at the posterior-lateral margin, yellow-grey, grading into the sole over several mm along the pressure zone, with fissures along the rim; no straight mask edge.

defects.what: Every nail ends in the same bright, even white strip on a uniformly pale, opaque pink plate, like a French manicure; at native size the five toes read as press-on nails with one treatment repeated.
defects.fix: Real toenail free edges are thin, off-white to yellowish and translucent, uneven in width, with grime beneath; the pink bed shows through the plate, and each toe's nail differs in tone, thickness and wear.

defects.what: No dorsal venous arch, no tributaries and no great saphenous vein in front of the medial malleolus read in any view (V1f, V2, V5f): the dorsum is smooth unveined skin, which on a lean man's foot reads as a mannequin.
defects.fix: A lean adult male foot shows a raised venous arch across the mid-dorsum with tributaries, and the great saphenous running up in front of the medial malleolus, soft 2.5-3.5 mm cords with a faint blue-green tint.

defects.what: The extensor tendons are thin hard-edged lines 1-2 mm wide fanning with even spacing over the dorsum, like wires or scored grooves under the skin, not cords; the EHL is no broader than the others.
defects.fix: Real extensors are soft rounded cords 3.5-5 mm wide (EHL broadest) that rise near the ankle and the MTPs and fade between, catching the rim light as broad soft highlights.

defects.what: One cloud-noise mottle of soft red and pale blotches 3-8 mm across covers dorsum, heel, ankle and sole at the same size and contrast: a procedural overlay, not perfusion, freckling or veins.
defects.fix: Real foot colour varies by region: redder toes and knuckles, paler yellower sole and heel, bluish veins, pigment at rub zones, with fine variation tied to pores, hair and creases.

defects.what: The medial midfoot is a smooth featureless ramp: no navicular knob, no abductor hallucis bulge, and the arch barely clears the floor; the lateral border likewise lacks the 5th MT styloid bump. The generic base-mesh look.
defects.fix: A real foot shows the navicular tuberosity and the arch clearly lifted between heel and ball on the medial side, the abductor's soft bulge below it, and the styloid as a sharp bump on the lateral border.

defects.what: The ball and toe bases carry one uniform field of parallel wavy ridges, the same pitch, depth and direction everywhere, like corduroy laid over the forms, unbroken by the ball and web creases.
defects.fix: Plantar ridges follow each region's own flow, flatten and wear on the weight-bearing ball, stop at the creases, and carry pores, dry scaling and fine wrinkles; pitch and depth vary.

defects.what: Toe 3 (and toe 4 at its base) is crossed by a ruler-straight hairline cut with a tone step across it, beige above and pink below: a seam between two pieces, not a flexion crease; it shows in V4 too.
defects.fix: A digital flexion crease is a curved soft fold with rounded lips, often doubled, that the ridges run into; tone and ridge flow continue across it.

defects.what: The hallux pad whorl is a perfect set of concentric ovals round one point, with a straight seam from the centre to the edge where the ridge phase jumps; the same target and seam recur on toes 2 and 3.
defects.fix: A real toe pad has a loop or whorl with ridge endings, bifurcations and a delta, uneven spacing and pores along the ridges; each toe differs, and nothing marks a radial seam.

defects.what: Thin brown stair-stepped outlines trace arcs over the plantar bases of toes 2-4 and the hallux where the pad texture region meets the sole's: an aliased mask edge printed on the skin.
defects.fix: No visible boundary: pad and sole skin blend through the plantar web crease, feathered over several mm, the change carried by real creases.

defects.what: The hallux plate sits on the toe like a glued acrylic tile: a crisp outline with skin merely butting against it, no lateral folds lapping over, a milky plate of one even tone with soft glossy blooms, and a free edge cut like plastic sheet.
defects.fix: A real plate sinks into lateral grooves under overlapping folds, shows the pink bed through translucent keratin with fine ridging and tone variation, and its free edge is thin, slightly ragged and translucent.

defects.what: A bright white crescent at the very base of the hallux plate, as bright and hard-edged as the free edge, reads as the plate's exposed proximal edge lifting off the skin, not as a lunula under a cuticle.
defects.fix: The proximal fold laps over the plate base with a thin cuticle; the lunula is a soft, slightly paler crescent seen through the plate just distal to the fold, never brighter than the free edge.

defects.what: From behind, the heel band's fissures are thin dark lines of constant width in a regular polygon net on a flat cream band, like crackle glaze, with no opening, depth or lifted flakes.
defects.fix: Real heel fissures are fewer and mostly run across the rim, open V-shaped with depth and a darker floor, with white dry flakes at their lips; plates vary in size and the band grades into the heel skin.

defects.what: The dorsum is bare; the only hairs are tight clumps of 2-8 short, straight, parallel dark strokes at the toe bases, like pen hatching, so the foot reads hairless and younger than a 40-year-old man's.
defects.fix: A man's dorsum carries sparse fine dark hairs scattered singly over its proximal half, lying flat toward the toes with random yaw, plus a loose tuft on the hallux's proximal phalanx.

ranked: [D1] The heel callus is the loudest tell: from below it is a cream decal over the whole heel pad, cut off by a ruler-straight edge and printed with an even crack net. Real callus is a raised rim band at the posterior-lateral margin that grades into the sole.

[D2] At native size every nail carries the same bright, even white free-edge strip on a pale opaque pink plate, a French manicure on five toes. Real toenail edges are thin, off-white to yellowish, uneven and often dirty underneath.

Overall the foot is too young and too clean for a boot-wearing 40-year-old soldier: even tone, no redness or darkening at the knuckles and rub points, no dryness or flaking. It reads as a silicone prosthetic, not a working man's foot.

[D3] No veins anywhere: no dorsal venous arch, no tributaries, no great saphenous in front of the medial malleolus. On a lean man's foot, as the anchor photos show, they are the most visible relief on the dorsum.

[D4] The extensor tendons are thin hard-edged lines 1-2 mm wide fanning at even spacing like wires under the skin; real extensors are soft cords 3.5-5 mm wide that rise near the ankle and the MTPs and fade between.

[D5] One cloud-noise mottle of red and pale blotches covers dorsum, heel, ankle and sole at the same size and contrast, an obvious procedural overlay; real colour changes by region and follows pores, veins and creases.

[D6] The medial midfoot is a smooth ramp with no navicular knob or abductor bulge and an arch that barely clears the floor, and the lateral border has no styloid bump: a generic base mesh, not a bony, articulated foot.

Toe skin is smooth and slightly waxy in V5f and hr.lesser: at 15-30 px/mm there is little cell or pore relief, and the knuckle creases are few and shallow where a man's toes show deep, darker wrinkles over each PIP.

Detail is sharp in one place and soft in the next: the plantar ridges are crisp and deep at 20 px/mm while the dorsum and toe tops at the same scale are nearly featureless, and the few hair strokes are pin-sharp on that soft skin.

[D7] The ball and toe bases carry one uniform field of parallel wavy ridges, same pitch, depth and direction everywhere, like corduroy, unbroken by the ball and web creases and unworn where the foot bears weight.
[D8] From below, toe 3 (and toe 4 at its base) is crossed by a ruler-straight hairline cut with a tone step across it, a seam between two pieces rather than a flexion crease; it shows even in V4.

[D9] Each toe pad's whorl is a perfect set of concentric ovals with a straight radial seam where the ridge phase jumps, the same target on every pad; real pads have loops and whorls with ridge endings, forks and pores.
[D10] Thin brown stair-stepped outlines trace arcs over the plantar toe bases where the pad texture region meets the sole's: an aliased mask edge drawn on the skin.

[D11] The hallux plate sits on the toe like a glued acrylic tile: crisp outline, no lateral folds lapping over it, a milky plate of one even tone with soft glossy blooms, and a free edge cut like plastic sheet of constant thickness.
[D12] A bright white crescent at the very base of the hallux plate, as bright as the free edge, reads as the plate's exposed proximal edge lifting off the skin, not as a lunula under a cuticle.

[D13] From behind, the heel band's fissures are thin dark lines of constant width in a regular polygon net on flat cream, a crackle glaze; real heel fissures are fewer, open, deeper and edged with white flakes.
[D14] The dorsum is bare; the only hairs are tight clumps of short, straight, parallel dark strokes at the toe bases, like pen hatching, which adds to the young, hairless read.
The lesser toes repeat one design, the same smooth cylinder, soft knuckle and pulp bulb at three sizes, so the row reads copy-pasted rather than four individual toes.

The back of the heel and ankle is mannequin-smooth: the Achilles is a faint ridge, there are no skin creases above the heel, and the malleoli read as soft swellings, not bony points with hollows around them.
